item.title: Gaza: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
item.description: Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Palestinians yearn for ‘a return to normal life’, says top Middle East peace envoy
item.description: The UN is continuing efforts to support Palestinians in Gaza amid major challenges to humanitarian access, reconstruction and the restoration of essential services, according to Ramiz Alakbarov, Acting UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Storm clouds over Gaza, deadly obstacles face Mexican women rights defenders, Latvia booze ban proves lifesaver
item.description: UN teams are racing to protect families in Gaza from the coming rainy season, but restricted access to land and shortages of critical supplies are hampering the effort, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Lebanon: One in five children goes to bed hungry, says UNICEF
item.description: Four in five households in Lebanon struggle to afford basic necessities today, with children increasingly going without food, missing school and being pushed into work as conflict compounds years of economic crisis. "I wanted to buy clothes for my children, but I could not. I also wanted to enrol them in school, but I could not afford that either," said one father of four, cited on Wednesday by the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen escalation fuels fears of further cholera, measles spread
item.description: Heavy fighting in Yemen is fuelling concerns of an uptick in cholera, measles and other preventable diseases, as overcrowding at displacement sites threatens to overwhelm the limited healthcare services still open.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Ambassadors meet as West Bank tensions rise, Gaza plan stalls
item.description: The Security Council met Monday morning with prospects for peace in the Middle East under strain on two fronts. In the West Bank, settler violence and settlement expansion are raising fears for a two-State solution. In Gaza, a year-old peace plan has stalled while civilian suffering continues. The meeting comes as the plan’s remaining phases, including Hamas’ disarmament and Israel’s full withdrawal, remain unimplemented, and as the illegality of settlements under international law remains a key point of contention.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Saudi Arabia warns Gulf security inseparable from global stability amid regional tensions
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister warned on Saturday that escalating threats across the Middle East risked international peace, energy security and global trade, calling for stronger international cooperation to protect Gulf States and vital shipping routes.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘No one speaks on behalf of Lebanon’: PM Salam asserts State authority at UN
item.description: Lebanon’s Prime Minister, Nawaf Salam, has stressed that decisions over war and peace, and control of weapons, must rest solely with the State and its constitutional institutions.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen violence deepens concerns over child hunger crisis
item.description: Aid agencies in Yemen highlighted the growing hunger emergency sparked by renewed fighting between Houthi opposition forces and Government troops, after mobile health clinics reported that hundreds of children displaced by the violence are suffering from the most deadly form of malnutrition.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UNRWA work and mandate in ‘jeopardy’, Guterres warns
item.description: The UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine refugees (UNRWA) continues to operate under “extraordinary pressure”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Palestinian existence under threat, Abbas tells UN, warning of ‘another Nakba’
item.description: Israeli policies now threaten “the very life and existence of the Palestinian people on their homeland”, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the UN General Assembly on Thursday, urging the world not to allow “another Nakba”.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: At UN, Pezeshkian turns terrorism accusation back on Iran’s critics
item.description: President Masoud Pezeshkian opened his General Assembly address with a direct rebuttal to US President Donald Trump, who a day earlier had branded Iran the “number one sponsor of terror.”
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Time is running out’ for Israel-Palestine two-State solution
item.description: The UN chief warned on Tuesday that the two-State solution for the Israel-Palestine conflict is at risk of collapse amid illegal Israeli settlement expansion and annexation.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Displacement on the rise in Yemen as fighting continues
item.description: As hostilities worsen in Yemen, more people have been fleeing their homes, further intensifying the humanitarian crisis within the region, the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN condemns attempted Houthi strike on Riyadh as Yemen displacement surges past 130,000
item.description: The UN has condemned continued cross‑border attacks by Houthi forces against Saudi Arabia, including an attempted strike on the capital Riyadh, as fighting inside Yemen drives one of the country’s fastest displacement surges in years.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen’s humanitarian crisis growing by the hour amid spike in displacement
item.description: People displaced by the renewed fighting in Yemen have described fleeing for their lives amid shelling and gunfire, aid agencies reported on Friday, while highlighting the dramatic increase in humanitarian needs in the country and in Djibouti, where thousands have sought shelter.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s transition in the spotlight
item.description: While Syria is making progress in its political transition, the Security Council is meeting to hear briefings and discuss the situation on the ground, including recent reports of deadly armed clashes with an ISIS-affiliate terrorist group in the south and protests over rising fuel prices.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen escalation displaces more than 57,000 children: UNICEF
item.description: Renewed fighting in Yemen is deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis in a country where more than 12 million children depend on aid, after more than a decade of conflict.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gaza: At least 20 killed in deadly building collapse, search for survivors continues
item.description: Search and rescue operations continued in Gaza City on Wednesday following the collapse of a bombed-out building that killed at least 20 people, according to reports.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Rising violence triggers emergency meeting on Yemen
item.description: Amid rising violence in Yemen, the Security Council met in emergency session on Tuesday to discuss the situation surrounding the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait shipping route as UN agencies warn of rising displacement, including thousands of Yemenis fleeing to Djibouti. UN News app users can follow here.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Escalating conflict drives new displacement in Yemen
item.description: The escalating conflict in Yemen is choking off aid shipments and driving fresh displacement, including to nearby Djibouti, with UN agencies reporting on Tuesday that nearly 100,000 people have been displaced since fighting intensified earlier this month.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gaza remains recovery points to possible war crimes, says UN rights chief
item.description: Bodies are still being pulled from the rubble of Gaza, three years after Israeli bombardment flattened entire neighbourhoods – most of them women and children.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Civilians bear the brunt, with deadly US strikes in Iran and thousands displaced in Yemen
item.description: Independent UN human rights investigators called for an immediate cessation of hostilities on Monday following a series of United States airstrikes on Iran in recent weeks that have killed civilians as tensions ripple through the region.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Married at 13, pregnant and starving: Child brides of Yemen
item.description: Fatimah* was 13 when she was married off to an older man. Two years later, she gave birth to twin daughters.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Where do we go?’: How Israel’s ‘yellow line’ is closing in on Palestinians
item.description: Ola Ishtiwi sits with her children in front of the remains of her home in the Al-Tuffah neighbourhood in eastern Gaza City, a few metres away from a series of painted cement blocks Israel has placed to mark what has become known as the “yellow line”.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Fresh attacks prompt emergency meeting on Yemen
item.description: On the heels of reported Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia on Tuesday and the capture of another key port by the militants on Yemen’s Red Sea coast – including the seizure of eight UN vehicles from a key aid hub there – the Security Council is meeting on Thursday at 3pm in New York to discuss the latest developments.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN chief demands Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon amid Nabatieh escalation
item.description: The Secretary-General has condemned mounting civilian casualties in southern Lebanon and called on Israel to withdraw its forces from Lebanese territory, as fighting intensifies in and around Nabatieh.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Syria’s transition hinges on justice for all, UN Human Rights Council hears
item.description: A successful and lasting transition in Syria requires comprehensive accountability, inclusion and guarantees that violations will not be repeated, UN independent investigators told the Human Rights Council in Geneva on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: In Gaza, women-headed households face ‘impossible choices’ to survive
item.description: In war-torn Gaza, a growing number of women-headed households face “impossible decisions” every day, amid ongoing Israeli airstrikes and still-scarce resources, UN humanitarians said on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI: Türk urges action before it becomes an ‘existential risk to humanity’
item.description: UN human rights chief Volker Türk added his voice on Monday to growing calls for greater AI controls, warning that the revolutionary technology could become an “existential risk to humanity” if left unchecked.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
